analysis.title: Lev Fin Weekend Reading + Observations: tricks and limited treats
key_insights: The FOMC left the fed funds target range unchanged at 3.75-4.00% at its October meeting, as expected.

A selloff in AI stocks snowballed into Friday's close, leaving the Nasdaq with its worst session since June and its largest monthly loss in more than a year. Every Magnificent Seven member closed down on Friday.

With 60% of S&P 500 companies reported, Q3'26 EPS growth is on track for 33% YoY, matching Q2 as the strongest quarter in recent decades outside post-recession recoveries. The Mag 7 are expected to report slower Q3 earnings growth than the rest of the S&P 500.
Credit had a quiet week at the index level: HY spreads were 3bps wider and loans 1bp tighter. HY primary was $4.44bn across 4 deals and only 3 benchmark-sized loans launched.
The Bloomberg US HY triple-C index OAS tightened 30bps to 1088bps on Tuesday, the first daily tightening of 30bps or more since February, then gave back 28bps by Friday's close.

25 HY index bonds fell 5+ points on the week, 12 of them rated triple-C or worse. 5.31% of the triple-C-or-lower bucket fell 5+ points last week versus 1.2% in a median week, and the share has been above 5% for four weeks.

The 6-week count of HY bonds falling 5+ points is 147, the second highest in 18 months behind the May-June 2025 selloff. Unlike May 2025, the median HY bond rose 0.28pts last week and the rest of the triple-C-or-lower bucket, excluding blow-ups, averaged a 1.06pt gain.
HY triple-Cs logged their first weekly gain in over two months and their best week since April. GS concludes that name selection matters more than triple-C beta.
US leveraged loans are up 3.04% YTD versus +0.60% for HY and -1.17% for IG. Last week 53 leveraged loans moved more than 3pts, a volatility similar to HY.
Loan funds posted their first weekly net outflow since the week ended June 24th. 62% of the distressed loan cohort is rated CCC+ or lower.
Single-Bs made up 24 of the 53 loan movers versus 22 for CCC+ or lower, and fell nearly as much on average (-1.01pts vs -1.04pts), so dispersion in loans extends beyond the deepest distressed tier.

Loan tailwinds: only $2.04bn of new loan deals launched last week, the lowest since the pre-Labor Day slowdown. Only 7.4% of the market trades at $100+, and when that share is 20% or less, median 6-month and 12-month returns have been higher since 2007.

53% of distressed loans mature within three years, the highest near-term maturity wall of any recent distressed peak. None of 2026's refinancings were for triple-C issuers, 31% were B-minus, and 4 of the 17 BSL-to-private-credit takeouts were triple-C.

Software is 32% of distressed loan volume versus a 12% index weight. GS says the cost of being wrong is as high as in recent memory and does not expect that to reverse through the rest of earnings season and into year-end.
Fitch's default rate across roughly 1,500 US private debt borrowers reached a record 6.3% in 3Q, up from 6.0% QoQ on an LTM basis.
Global publicly syndicated bond issuance passed the 2025 annual record of $6.61tn with two months left in the year.
Procter & Gamble priced a $4bn four-part deal including a 30-year tranche at +60bps over USTs, the tightest 30-year spread in more than two decades.
HY AI issuers widened back out to 389bp by week end versus non-AI BB/B at 263bp.

GS Oil Analyst raised its December Brent forecast to $105/bbl from $90 and WTI to $94, and its 2027 average forecasts to $88 Brent (from $80) and $78 WTI (from $73), citing high supply disruption risks.
GS reading list includes a US Economics Analyst preview of the midterm elections, which are this week, and a US Daily recap describing an every-other-meeting pace for the Fed.

tension_points.bull_case: HY triple-Cs had their first weekly gain in over two months and best week since April, the OAS tightened 30bps in a day, and the median HY bond rose 0.28pts with the rest of the triple-C bucket averaging +1.06pts.
tension_points.bear_case: 5.31% of the triple-C-or-lower bucket fell 5+ points versus 1.2% in a median week, 147 bonds have fallen 5+ points over six weeks, and the Tuesday tightening was mostly given back by Friday.

tension_points.bull_case: Loans are up 3.04% YTD, new supply was only $2.04bn, and with only 7.4% of the market at $100+, historical median returns have been higher.
tension_points.bear_case: Loan funds had their first net outflow since June 24th, 53 loans moved more than 3pts, and 53% of distressed loans mature within three years with narrow refinancing exits.

theme_stances.key_argument: Selection matters more than beta because distressed loans face a near-term maturity wall, narrow refinancing exits and heavy software exposure.
The index-level triple-C rally masks a share of bonds falling 5+ points that is running at more than four times the median-week rate.
theme_stances.evidence: picking the right names matters more in this market
